#1695. Liverpool injury news: Reds receive fresh Dominik Szoboszlai update ahead of Man United clash

By Ben Sully | 17 Nov 2026 00:33, Last updated: 17 Nov 2026 00:33

Hungary boss Marco Rossi has insisted Liverpool midfielder Dominik Szoboszlai is fit to play in Tuesday's UEFA Nations League clash against Northern Ireland.

Szoboszlai was forced off with a minor knee issue in Liverpool's 3-1 win over Crystal Palace before the international break.

As a result, there was some doubt as to whether he would link up with the Hungary squad for the final two matches of the Nations League league phase.

Not only did he join up with his national team, but he played the full duration of Saturday's 2-0 away win over Georgia, in which he provided an assist for Barnabas Varga's 85th-minute effort.

Szoboszlai revealed after the match that he was close to pulling out of the game after feeling the injury in the pre-match warm-up.

The midfielder also said his leg "felt good" during the game and that he would start the "treatment process all over again" in a bid to be ready for Tuesday's home meeting with Northern Ireland.

Speaking in Monday's pre-match press conference, Rossi attempted to ease fears over Szoboszlai's injury status, insisting his captain is ready to feature at the Puskas Arena.

“Have you noticed problems in the previous matches? In Georgia?” Rossi said.

“I didn’t see any problem in Dominik. He played like he is usually going to play so for us there is no problem, he is available.

“I don’t think the situation is affecting him too much and you can see clearly by the performance. I don’t think we have anything to complain about his performance in Georgia.”

For Hungary, Tuesday's game is an important fixture as it offers the chance to secure promotion to League A of the Nations League.

Having collected 10 points from their five matches, Hungary enter the final matchday in second spot and one point behind leaders Northern Ireland in Group B2.

Meanwhile, Liverpool's main priority is Sunday's Premier League clash against Manchester United, who will start life under new head coach Mauricio Pochettino.

Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola will be keen to have Szoboszlai available for the home fixture, especially as there is doubt over Ryan Gravenberch's availability.

#1694. 'I feel betrayed, misled, in shock. It was a stupid thing for them to do': ANDY WOODMAN relives the moment he was 'brutally' sacked by Bromley - and how his best mate Sir Gareth Southgate helped him cope

Published: 21:00 EST, 9 November 2026 | Updated: 05:29 EST, 11 November 2026

Every sacked manager has a sob story – but few dismissals have felt as harsh as Bromley’s recent decision to part ways with Andy Woodman.

Pound for pound, no club has outperformed their history, budget and expectations in English football across the last decade as much as Bromley. But after an understandably tricky start in League One – two wins from their first 10 games – Woodman was shown the door.

In his first interview since that decision last month, the 55-year-old tells Daily Mail Sport about feelings of 'betrayal' and 'shock' before making his pitch to future employers. But the most eye-opening part of our candid conversation comes when I ask the man with more than four decades of experience to recall the club he took over in 2021.

‘Look, Bromley is your classic non-League club,’ says Woodman. ‘I mean that with the greatest respect to all non-League clubs and I hate the word “non-League” as I think it should be “League Three”, as they are all professional.

‘But the facilities are non-League, the mentality is non-League. Everything is done day-to-day, hand-to-mouth, every penny counts, every decision that costs money counts, it is run by people’s personal money.

‘It was tough when I started: we had no turnstiles, no club shop, we trained on the pitch because it was astroturf, we had no gym.’

Andy Woodman was sacked as Bromley boss last month despite leading the club to the FA Trophy in 2022, promotion to the Football League in 2024 and then another promotion to League One last season

Woodman with the FA Trophy in 2022. 'Every manager who gets sacked, we all have a story of hardship to tell and all feel it is unfair,' says the former Bromley boss

Under chairman Robin Stanton-Gleaves, Woodman and Co, Bromley changed this mentality and shot up the pyramid, winning the FA Trophy in 2022, promotion to the Football League in 2024 and then another promotion to League One last season. Two months later, it was all over.

Asked how he feels about the decision, Woodman, who used to coach in the Arsenal academy system, says: ‘Yeah, I feel betrayed. Every manager who gets sacked, we all have a story of hardship to tell and all feel it is unfair. That’s fine, I get how the football business works.

‘But the bit that didn't sit comfortably with me was the conversations I was having with people at the club or owners, everyone above me… there was no inkling of any of this. I feel misled. I was surprised.

‘One day, we were talking about plans and the way forward and how to get through this sticky little period with players out injured, then the next minute it was a change of direction. Nothing like, “Right, you’ve got three games to turn it round”, none of that, nothing.

‘My record was good there, the owner always said if anyone can churn out results it was myself. Football has no patience. In football, people always forget where they come from. I understand wanting to move forward. It’s disappointing really, that’s the best word I can use. I feel let down.

‘It was just a normal day when they told me. I was going into training, popped across to where the chairman’s office was and then was just told, “We are going to take a change of direction”. It was no more than that, I didn’t try to change the decision or ask why.

‘It was a two-minute conversation, it didn’t need more than that really. I went to tell the staff and went home! It sounds brutal and it is… I am sure people will read this and think, “You deserve this” and “You deserve that” but what else can you do? There’s no easy way of doing it.

'When you have been told you are sacked, you don’t really want to stick around and have a long conversation. They didn’t give an explanation. They needed results, they said. We lost to Leicester which was not a great result, obviously. But realistically they are Leicester… and we are Bromley.’

'It was a two-minute conversation, it didn’t need more than that really. I went to tell the staff and went home! It sounds brutal and it is'

Woodman, who used to be the Arsenal youth team goalkeeping coach, says: 'When I left Bromley that day, I just felt in shock to be really honest'

To hammer home that last point: Woodman’s first game was against Wealdstone in April 2021 in the National League at Hayes Lane. On that same weekend, Leicester were hosting soon-to-be champions Manchester City. Oh, and the Foxes won the FA Cup a month later.

‘When I left that day, I just felt in shock to be honest,’ continues Woodman. ‘I felt the next three games were winnable. I had played seven of the top 10 teams, beaten the top team Huddersfield, my goalie was just coming back from injury and some others were coming back.

‘We had two teams in the bottom four and one just outside so I felt it was my best opportunity to get some much-needed results.

‘To take someone out who has been in football 40 years and been in coaching 25 years and then to put (his former assistant) Byron Webster in charge who had just been fresh out of playing and has never done a coaching session… with every respect, it feels unfair to him. It was a stupid thing to do. I found that really strange, they took one point from those three games. It fascinates me.’

Now, with Bromley bottom of League One, Karl Robinson, the former Salford and MK Dons boss, has taken over. Woodman, though, is keen not to sound bitter and will remember his five-and-a-half years at the club with fondness. He says his best memories are taking Bromley into the Football League, playing at Newcastle in the FA Cup and beating ‘Hollywood Netflix club Wrexham’ in the FA Trophy final.

Sir Gareth Southgate remains his best friend, the pair having met as teenagers in the Crystal Palace academy. They took turns in being best man at each other’s wedding and Southgate is godfather of goalkeeper Andy’s son Freddie, who is on Liverpool’s books.

They also co-authored the 2004 book Woody and Nord which chronicles two polar opposite career paths that started at the same level, one going on to play (and later manage) England, the other a journeyman in the lower leagues.

‘Nothing surprises Gareth and I,’ adds Woodman. ‘We have been in the game for 40 years now. You can argue that in his tenure at England, he got them as high as they have ever been in 60 years and it still was not enough. So it doesn’t surprise us. People have to make decisions and they are business-related, only time will tell if it is the right decision but that’s not my problem any more.

Woodman and lifelong friend Sir Gareth Southgate at the release of their 2004 book 'Woody and Nord' which charts two very different careers in football

Southgate is godfather to Woodman's son Freddie, a goalkeeper on Liverpool's books

‘Gareth was very supportive, so was Alan Pardew and the support from the Premier League right down to the National League, there has been no end of messages I have had, which is comforting.

‘That first Saturday after being out, I didn’t want to be watching or listening to the game, I just wanted to get away because that is the worst. I have had two clubs ring me, there are ongoing conversations and I am just making sure it is the right vehicle for me. What I mean by that is I want an owner that is aligned and who thinks they can compete to get out of their league.

‘My record speaks for itself. If you ask most managers how many promotions and trophies they have won, I bet over long careers, they haven’t got many. For me, with the smallest budget in the leagues, we maximised the team and maximised success.

‘To get two promotions and an FA Trophy win against Wrexham, hitting the play-offs four times in five years, that is something I am really proud of. If nothing else, the Bromley supporters and town are grateful.’

#1693. Opinion: Massive Real Madrid to Liverpool deal looks increasingly possible

Real Madrid appear ready to open the door to a massive sale. Liverpool can swoop in here and get themselves a proper star.

Liverpool need to invest in their midfield. That should be obvious to everyone now after a start to the season that demonstrated an incredible weakness there.

That's the result of building a midfield group entirely out of attacking players. All of Liverpool's options want to get further forward, leaving no one to really cover gaps or stop counter-attacks.

It's led to Andoni Iraola calling on Trey Nyoni to learn the holding role but even he is better known as a more advanced midfielder. It also just means that Liverpool are essentially relying on a teenager to keep their side secure - hardly ideal.

We fully expect Liverpool to move for a defensive, controlling midfielder in 2027. Maybe that's in January or maybe it's in the summer but either way, some sort of move simply must be on the way.

Real Madrid look ready to do businessThere's a midfielder we have our eyes on at Real Madrid: Eduardo Camavinga. He's been heavily linked to Liverpool in the past and his situation in Madrid is becoming less and less clear. Or rather, it's becoming more clear that he's not viewed as a long-term piece. #1690. Max Dowman achieves historic England Under-21s feat as Arsenal youngster breaks another Jude Bellingham record

By Ben Sully | 17 Nov 2026 01:09, Last updated: 17 Nov 2026 04:00

Arsenal youngster Max Dowman became England Under-21s' youngest-ever goalscorer in Monday's 3-2 win over France.

After making 13 appearances for England's Under-19 side, Dowman earned his first call-up to the Under-21 squad for the current international window.

The 16-year-old became the youngest player to represent England Under-21s when he featured as a substitute in the 1-0 defeat against Portugal in Friday's friendly at Ashton Gate, surpassing the record previously held by Jude Bellingham.

Dowman was then given the chance to start Monday's friendly against France, and he made the most of his opportunity, scoring an 89th-minute winner after England had spurned a two-goal lead.

The winning goal ✨ Max Dowman has his first goal for our #YoungLions! https://t.co/gb4rLaXXBV

Everton's Harrison Armstrong created the winner, stealing possession high up the pitch before squaring the ball for Dowman to steer home a simple left-foot finish.

As a result of the effort, Dowman took another record away from Bellingham as he became England Under-21s' youngest-ever scorer.

Dowman found the net at the age of 16 years and 320 days old, surpassing the record Bellingham set when he scored on his Under-21s debut against Kosovo at the age of 17 years and 67 days in September 2020.

The Arsenal academy product also picked up the Player of the Match award as he helped Carsley's side end a three-game winless run.

The winning goal and your #YoungLions Player of the Match connected by @EE! ? Max Dowman ? https://t.co/eNmPkLLWVN

In regard to the England Under-21s, Dowman will hope to be part of the squad that heads to Albania and Serbia next summer for the European Under-21 Championship.

In the short term, the winger will link back up with his Arsenal teammates, who will prepare for Saturday's Premier League away clash against Newcastle United.

However, he will be unable to feature against the Magpies as he serves the final match of the three-game ban he received following his red card in the EFL Cup defeat against Fleetwood Town.

Dowman could return to the squad for the Champions League clash against Borussia Dortmund on November 24, just days before the Gunners take on Manchester City in the Premier League.

#1685. “We needed to make a move” – Moncada explains Milan’s multi-year pursuit of Cisse

Geoffrey Moncada, today, has given a bit of insight into how long AC Milan were trying to sign Alphadjo Cisse.

When Milan signed Cisse, there was a bit of a mixed reaction. Although he was seen as a talent for the future, the money could’ve been spent on a first-team acquisition, with the squad lacking in certain areas.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Now, though, everyone would be glad that the decision was made to sign the young Italian. To say he’s exploded this season would be an understatement and he’s perhaps the biggest gem at the club right now.

Speaking to Calcio e Pepe, as Francesco Nasato relayed on X, Moncada went through the process of the Rossoneri’s scouting of Cisse.

“We had a scout who worked near Verona and he immediately pointed out this boy to us, Alphadjo Cisse, who played for the Under-17s and then for the Primavera, and then for the Under-20s. So we went to see him and he was very interesting.

“Two or three years ago, we launched Milan Futuro. Our idea was to sign him for that team a year earlier, but we couldn’t reach an agreement with Hellas Verona. They wanted to keep him and decided to send him on loan to Serie B.

“We followed him very closely in Serie B, too, and he literally exploded there in the first six months. We told ourselves he’d made such a good transition from the Primavera and Verona’s bench to Serie B that we needed to make a move.

“It was winter and we had to hurry. If he had gone to PSV and you had wanted to buy him later, perhaps after playing in the Champions League, the price would have risen to €30 or €40 million. Sometimes you have to speed things up a bit.”

Considering the club had followed him since he was in the Under-17s, it’s a good thing they eventually managed to sign him, especially with the way he’s started at San Siro.

The final playoff game on the Western Conference side will take place Thursday as the Seattle Sounders host Real Salt Lake in the MLS Wild Card Round at Lumen Field.

These teams wound up eighth and ninth in the West during the regular season, with the Rave Green defeating Los Angeles FC the last time out 2-1, putting them a point above Salt Lake, who won by that same score on Decision Day against the Los Angeles Galaxy.

It was an underwhelming regular season overall for Seattle, but they managed to get a result when needed to keep their campaign alive.

While they finished with nine fewer points this year than in 2025, Brian Schmetzer’s men found a way to stay above the playoff line by the skin of their teeth.

They have dropped points in five of their last six games but have won more playoff encounters than any MLS club (26) since their debut season in the league in 2009.

In 2026, the Sounders lost four more home games (five) than the year before, though they have only lost one playoff match at Lumen Field this decade in normal time, with Los Angeles FC blanking them 1-0 in 2023.

This will be the first time they compete in the Wild Card Round, with the Rave Green winning their first post-season home outing in 2025.

The Sounders are unbeaten in their last four MLS home games versus Real Salt Lake, collecting a clean sheet on three of those occasions.

Like Seattle, Salt Lake came up big when needed on Decision Day, qualifying for the post-season for a sixth consecutive time.

While Pablo Mastroeni has never missed the playoffs since taking charge of this team in 2021, they lost their only Wild Card outing last year at the Portland Timbers (3-1).

On Thursday, RSL will try to end a four-match playoff losing run and win their first post-season game away from home since upsetting Sporting Kansas City 2-1 in 2021.

During the 2026 MLS campaign, Claret and Cobalt were pointless in their three away outings against the Cascadia clubs (the Portland Timbers, Vancouver Whitecaps and Sounders), netting just one goal overall against those teams.

Entering this must-win game, however, the club from Sandy, Utah have won two of their last three MLS away encounters.

Their recent playoff form may not be great, but RSL have won their last two knockout matches against Seattle across all competitions, upsetting them on penalties at Lumen Field in the opening round of the 2021 MLS Cup playoffs.

Seattle Sounders Major League Soccer form:

Both Alex Roldan and Danny Musovski will be questionable for the Sounders on Thursday, with the former recovering from a calf strain and the latter from a head injury.

A knee problem will likely keep Nikola Petkovic out as well, while Yeimar Gomez Andrade has a sore hamstring and Pedro de la Vega is doubtful with a quad issue.

Albert Rusnak and Sebastian Gomez netted first-half goals which were ultimately just enough to earn them a win against LAFC.

As for Real Salt Lake, Diego Luna and Emeka Eneli are both unlikely to feature in this upcoming fixture due to knee injuries.

There were several new faces in their starting 11 on Decision Day, with Kobi Henry and Zach Booth among those being inserted on the backline.

Sergi Solans and Booth found the back of the net early versus the Galaxy, while an own goal from Luc de Fougerolles led to some anxious moments in the second half before the final whistle blew.

Thomas; Kossa-Rienzi, Kee-hee, Ragen, Tolo; Dotson, C. Roldan; Morris, Rusnak, Ferreira; Joveljic

Cabral; Sanabria, Glad, De Fougerolles, Quinton, Booth; Guilavogui, Caliskan, Spierings, Lobjanhidze; Solans

#1681. Taking instructions from a schoolboy and showing class at half-pace... William Saliba made impressive injury comeback for Arsenal Under-21s - now he faces fight to take Ezri Konsa's spot, writes ISAAN KHAN

Published: 06:24 EST, 11 November 2026 | Updated: 06:28 EST, 11 November 2026

It was a scene straight out of Will Ferrell's Elf. In the middle of Arsenal's Under-21 team huddle stood William Saliba, all 6ft 4in of him, towering over his teenage team-mates as 17-year-old captain Marli Salmon delivered his pre-match rallying cry.

One of the world's finest defenders was taking instructions from a schoolboy.

For the hundreds of Arsenal supporters who had descended on Boreham Wood's Meadow Park on Sunday, it was an extraordinary sight. Four months after suffering a back injury in France's World Cup semi-final defeat by Spain, Saliba was finally back on a football pitch.

But his carefully managed 45-minute appearance in a 5-2 victory over Aston Villa's Under-21s marked the beginning of another challenge. Saliba must now win back a place in an Arsenal defence which, remarkably, has barely missed him.

That is largely down to Ezri Konsa, the £55million summer signing from Aston Villa who has been so impressive in Saliba's absence that Mikel Arteta faces a genuine selection dilemma.

Saliba and Gabriel have been Arsenal's established central defensive partnership since the opening day of the 2022-23 season. But Konsa, arguably Arsenal's outstanding defender this term, has made a compelling case to keep his place.

William Saliba towered over his teenage team-mates and played 45 minutes on Sunday

His performance in the 1-0 victory at Liverpool, Arsenal's first win at Anfield in 14 years, was particularly impressive. He won every ground duel, made 14 defensive contributions and completed eight clearances, leading the match statistics in all three categories. Liverpool failed to register a shot on target.

It was precisely the sort of performance that has given Arteta something to think about. And the Arsenal manager is understood to have challenged Konsa to fight for his place rather than simply make way for the returning Frenchman.

There is another solution. Konsa can operate at right back, a position he has occupied for both Villa and England, including during the summer's World Cup. That would allow Arteta to restore the Saliba-Gabriel partnership without sacrificing a player who has become such an important part of Arsenal's defence. For now, however, there will be no rush.

Saliba's injury history explains why Arsenal have been so careful. In 2022-23, another back problem kept him out for 97 days and contributed significantly to the collapse of a title challenge that had seen the club spend 248 days at the top of the Premier League.

Arsenal have since finished runners-up again and finally claimed the title last summer, but the lessons of that earlier setback have not been forgotten.

Leading back specialists were consulted over Saliba's latest injury before the club settled on a conservative rehabilitation programme, deliberately extending his recovery rather than risking another setback.

He returned to full first-team training last Tuesday, ahead of Arsenal's 2-1 victory over Slavia Prague, but Sunday's appearance represented his first competitive action since July. His absence from France's squad during the international break should allow Arsenal to continue building his fitness without interruption.

And there was plenty to suggest that the long wait has done little to diminish his quality.

The Frenchman is building up his fitness after four months on the sidelines

Saliba faces a tough test to try and break up the partnership formed by Gabriel and Ezri Konsa

Playing comfortably within himself, Saliba repeatedly strolled past opponents before threading passes through the Villa midfield. At times he ventured so far forward after set-pieces that supporters began joking about whether he fancied himself as a centre-forward.

Even at half-pace, the gulf between a world-class defender and academy football was obvious.

Yet it was Saliba's interaction with his young team-mates that provided some of the afternoon's most revealing moments.

Throughout the first half he could be heard directing Salmon, shouting 'man on,' 'high, high' and 'well done, Marli' as he guided his teenage defensive partner through the game.

When Arsenal scored their opening goal, Salmon initially stayed back rather than joining the celebrations. Saliba promptly ordered him forward to enjoy the moment.

Marli Salmon, pictured laying a wreath for Remembrance Day, was the one barking out instructions and seeing Saliba (left) among the youngsters was an extraordinary sight

It was a small gesture but typical of the interest Saliba has taken in Arsenal's younger players during his rehabilitation.

He is understood to have spent time asking about their families and offering advice about life in professional football.

One particular message has been the importance of looking after their parents if they are fortunate enough to make a successful career in the game. The affection is clearly mutual.

Children clamoured for autographs as Saliba arrived and departed, while Arsenal had prepared for the unusual attention surrounding an Under 21 fixture.

Large QR codes directing spectators to the team line-up had been displayed around the ground and a member of the first-team security staff accompanied Saliba between the dressing room and the pitch.

His afternoon was meticulously choreographed. At half-time, his work completed, he disappeared into the changing rooms before leaving through a side exit.

Saliba made his comeback for Arsenal's Under 21 side after a long injury absence

The 45 minutes will have provided reassurance to Arteta and Arsenal's medical staff, as well as a memorable afternoon for the teenagers who shared the pitch with him. For Saliba, though, the real work is only beginning.

Few would have imagined when he suffered his injury in July that he might return to find his place under threat. Konsa's performances have changed that calculation.

Arsenal have their defensive cornerstone back. Now Arteta must decide what to do with him.

#1677. Orlando City vs FC Cincinnati - prediction, team news, lineups

By Joel Lefevre | 17 Nov 2026 02:52

With a spot in the opening phase of the MLS Cup playoffs up for grabs, Orlando City will welcome FC Cincinnati to Inter.com Stadium in the Sunshine State on Thursday for that Wild Card matchup.

The Lions finished the regular season eighth, blanking the New England Revolution 1-0 in their last meeting, with Cincy below them after a 2-0 Decision Day home defeat to Nashville SC.

A season that appeared headed for disaster in the spring came to life in the late summer as Orlando City recovered and climbed back above the playoff line.

The arrival of Antoine Griezmann changed their fortunes dramatically, with nine of this club’s 13 wins coming after the 2018 World Cup winner arrived.

Martin Perelman’s men are unbeaten in their last seven MLS outings at home, dropping points on only one of those occasions.

On Thursday they can collect their first post-season triumph since the 2024 Eastern Conference semi-finals when they blanked Atlanta United 1-0.

Orlando have won six straight league contests at home when netting the opening goal and have never lost a playoff game on home soil when doing so.

Thanks in part to Griezmann’s presence, the Lions rose to eighth in the league regarding average goals per game (1.9) in 2026.

In a win-and-in scenario on Decision Day, Cincinnati failed to deliver, ending a four-match domestic unbeaten run and setting up this Wild Card showdown.

A defeat on Thursday would mark the first time that the Orange and Blue fail to feature in the first round of the playoffs since Pat Noonan took charge ahead of the 2022 campaign.

Cincinnati have points in three successive MLS away encounters and have lost just one of their last five games domestically as the visitors.

They have never won a post-season away game in 90 minutes, with their only such triumph occurring in New Jersey in 2023 on penalties versus the New York Red Bulls.

They averaged the fourth-most goals per match in the league this past season (2.0) but conceded the third-most per game (2.2) just slightly fewer than Orlando City, who were second from the bottom in that department (2.3).

The Orange and Blue are unbeaten in their last four MLS meeting versus Orlando City, while Noonan has never lost a match against them at Inter.co Stadium.

Due to a back injury, Griffin Dorsey is questionable for Orlando City, while foot issues are likely to keep Tyrese Spicer and Robin Jansson out of the fold on Thursday and Iago Teodoro is eligible to return from his suspension.

Braian Ojeda had the only goal against New England on Decision Day while Maxime Crepeau collected his fifth clean sheet of the campaign.

#1676. Sergio Navarro’s style and the key individuals: Milan Futuro tactical analysis

Milan Futuro decided to go in a new direction this summer by appointing Sergio Navarro, but is it working so far?

Milan launched the Futuro project ahead of the 2024-25 season. with the aim of creating a pathway for academy players to break into the first team. The project was designed to bridge the physical and technical gap between the Primavera and senior football.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Things didn’t go well in year one, as Daniele Bonera didn’t see out the season as the head coach. He recently stated he didn’t think the squad was ready for the level, and ultimately Massimo Oddo was unable to save the team from relegation to Serie D, the fourth tier of Italian football.

With promotion back to Serie C the objective, this summer the Rossoneri turned to Sergio Navarro, a coach with good pedigree in Spain. The Futuro now appear to have a clearer structure, a defined playing identity and the right guidance, as Rohit Rajeev has outlined.

Under Barquero, Milan Futuro operate in a 4-2-3-1 formation. Asanji leads the line, with Ossola playing as the number 10 and Vos and Guernier occupying the wide positions.

Plazotta and Pandolfi form the double pivot, while Cisse and Pagliei partner at centre-back, with Perera and Colombo completing the back four.

Milan Futuro favour a possession-oriented approach, circulating the ball patiently at a measured tempo while waiting for gaps to emerge in the opposition’s defensive structure. They also use passing triangles effectively to create short passing options and play through the opposition’s high press.

In possession, Milan Futuro adopt a 3-1-6 structure, with Barquero showing little hesitation in committing players forward to create numerical overloads in the opposition half.

Asanji positions himself just behind the opposition’s defensive line, keeping the centre-backs occupied and preventing them from stepping forward freely. Meanwhile, Pandolfi and Plazotta maintain parallel positions in the double pivot, providing a stable base for the attacking structure.

In the opposition half, Milan Futuro keep the distances between players very short, allowing them to combine through quick, one-touch passes.

This also helps them create ball-sided overloads, with two or three players surrounding the Milan player in possession to provide close passing options. Once they enter the opposition half, the tempo increases as Milan look to become more direct and progress towards goal.

Similar to Amorim’s approach at Sporting, Milan Futuro form vertical corridors with three players positioned one behind another. This structure facilitates quick passing combinations while also creating movement to manipulate the opposition.

When Milan players drop to form these corridors or create overloads, they often drag defenders with them, opening spaces elsewhere to exploit.

Milan Futuro look to press the opposition high up the pitch, adopting a 4-4-2 shape with a man-oriented pressing scheme. This allows them to put pressure on the opposition’s build-up and restrict the time and space available to play out from the back.

Milan Futuro also set up pressing traps by deliberately leaving the opposition’s wide player unmarked. The pass towards the wide player acts as the pressing trigger, prompting Milan’s players to jump out of their positions and aggressively close down the receiver, while cutting off the available passing options.

Milan Futuro maintain an extremely narrow defensive shape, prioritising the protection of central spaces and forcing the opposition towards the flanks.

Once the opposition attempts to progress through the wide areas, the press shifts across to create numerical overloads around the ball, while Guernier and Colombo provide cover and prevent the opposition from switching play to the opposite flank.

Perhaps the most important aspect of Barquero’s approach is his willingness to build the system around his players’ strengths and allow them the freedom to express themselves.

Rather than focusing solely on tactical adaptability, he appears equally committed to their individual development and helping them grow as footballers. Here are a few examples.

One of Milan Futuro’s methods of chance creation is to play direct passes into Asanji. His ability to position himself between the ball and the opposition defender, using his physicality to shield possession and hold up play, is crucial to this approach.

Rather than asking him to adapt to the role of a more technically oriented, ball-playing striker, Barquero has built a mechanism that makes the most of his existing strengths.

Perhaps the clearest demonstration of Barquero’s coaching ability is his utilisation of Vos and Guernier. Guernier is a natural winger/forward, while Vos is more accustomed to playing as an attacking midfielder.

Within the 3-1-6 structure, Vos often inverts from the left flank into an inside-left role, allowing Perera to provide the width.

At times, he is also given the freedom to interchange positions with Plazotta, allowing him to drop into midfield or advance further up the pitch. This positional freedom helps him develop his midfield qualities and realise his potential.

Guernier, meanwhile, tends to maintain his width, stretching the opposition’s defensive line and creating space for Vos and the other attackers to exploit.

Barquero also gives Guernier the freedom to take on his direct opponent, even when he is outnumbered, allowing him to use his dribbling ability without being restricted by the team’s structure.

Ossola, who is particularly effective at receiving between the lines and turning with the ball, is allowed to operate higher up the pitch, closer to the opposition’s defensive line.

Idrissi, on the other hand, prefers to receive possession deeper, where he can dictate play with his passing range or carry the ball forward through dribbling.

#1675. Report - Barcelona told no: Amazing star picks Liverpool and he's ready to sign

Barcelona have been told no - one amazing star wants to join Liverpool. He's ready and waiting to agree a deal with the Reds.

Liverpool’s defence needs work. The Reds aren’t happy with what they’ve got and change will be forced on them purely through contract situations. The biggest of those being Virgil van Dijk.

The Dutchman is out of contract next summer. We hope Liverpool renew the deal but he’ll also turn 36 ahead of the 2027/28 campaign. There is every chance that the Reds just let him walk away.

Joe Gomez, too, is out of contract. It would be a massive surprise if he re-signed, given his injury history, and that would force Liverpool into some difficult squad decisions as they’d lose yet another homegrown player.

Add in the bizarre right-back situation where Conor Bradley is out long-term and Jeremie Frimpong simply isn’t trusted. Liverpool have very little on their books guaranteed next season - but they do at least have one semi-guarantee.

Ronald Araujo is currently on loan from Barcelona, so he's not actually certain to be with the squad beyond this campaign. Though, there is a buy clause for €55m that could change things.

And Marca reports that Araujo would sign for Liverpool if they triggered it. He's ready to turn down a return to Barcelona, picking a long-term future with the Reds over taking a step backwards.

That's golden news for Liverpool. Araujo is someone who helps significantly with both the centre-back and right-back problem areas, as we've seen already this season. He's also a very experienced player - something Liverpool desperately need as currently, the only centre-backs guaranteed to be with the squad next season are Jeremy Jacuqet (22) and Giovanni Leoni (19).

Now, it's important to note that things could change. Liverpool can't trigger their buy option until the end of the season and perhaps Araujo has a change of heart by then. Even if that feels unlikely at this stage.

Because as things stand, he wants to stay with Liverpool. We think it will ultimately prove to be a sensible signing a real win for the squad in what looks like a complicated summer.

#1673. Man United transfer news: Two Nico Paz demands could rule out Red Devils move

By Axel Clody | 17 Nov 2026 06:14

Midfielder Nico Paz could leave Como in 2027, and Manchester United are mentioned as a possible destination for the Argentine. But he has demands that could be problematic for the club.

Author of a fine season with his club so far - 14 matches, six goals and eight assists - the 22-year-old attacking midfielder is already setting the 2027 transfer market alight. Real Madrid are the favourites to bring him back, thanks to their £68m (€80m) buy-back clause, but PSG could still take advantage, while Manchester United are thinking of Paz as a dream replacement for Bruno Fernandes.

But the expectations of the 15-cap international for his future club could mean Paris disappear from the equation.

According to information shared by The Touchline, Paz has two demands for the rest of his career and his future club.

The first is that the club in question play in the Champions League, and do so consistently. That could rule out Manchester United, as the English club, who have just appointed Mauricio Pochettino, are currently 18th in the Premier League.

The second is a guarantee of a place in the starting XI. Here it is with PSG that this could weigh: as Luis Enrique has repeated on several occasions in the past, the two-time European champions do not promise any player a place in the starting XI.

All the more so as the Spanish manager readily practises rotation, even if some players are obviously more regular starters than others.

Still young (22), Paz left Real Madrid in 2024 to make a name for himself in Italy and then in Europe with Como.

Very early on, then, the Argentine put playing time ahead of everything else: a move to Como could represent a sporting gamble, as the Italian club, although backed by a billionaire, had just been promoted to Serie A.

For the rest of his career, therefore, the playmaker intends to be attentive to his playing time, even if his talent, now recognised, naturally opens doors for him.

But not necessarily those of PSG, where competition is fierce in attack and in midfield. The same goes for Real Madrid: can Como’s number 10 oust Jude Bellingham as the central attacking midfielder at Real? Not so sure... Could that also call into question a possible future in Madrid?

#1671. Soccer hooligans descend on Australia: Wild footage shows horde of fans smashing cars and damaging property

Published: 03:01 EST, 9 November 2026 | Updated: 07:38 EST, 11 November 2026

Shocking footage of soccer fans after a match has reignited complaints about public safety, following previous warnings repeated violence was putting families at risk.

Perth Glory supporters have demanded action over a confrontation near HBF Park, with video posted on social media showing a group of young people as they crowded around a parked white vehicle and aggressively rocked it from side to side.

Other footage filmed from across the road shows young people confronting fans in the street, with the group spread across the footpath and roadway outside nearby businesses.

Images shared alongside the complaints show fighting on previous occasions, as well as damaged fences and other property. Supporters allege the material documents a recurring problem involving the same group and have demanded bans and stronger security measures.

The footage prompted calls for bans and renewed criticism of matchday security, with supporters alleging genuine fans face strict enforcement over minor issues while more serious behaviour goes unchecked.

'The same group of troublemakers causing chaos and mobbing random people', one fan posted on social media platform X.

Young people crowd around a parked white car and aggressively rock it near HBF Park in footage that has sparked anger among Perth Glory supporters

Supporters allege genuine fans are being left feeling unsafe at Perth Glory matches

Tagging Perth Glory, they added: 'It's time you do something about it. People have had enough.'

The supporter also called for individuals to be banned and, in a subsequent post, alleged nearby property had been damaged.

WA Police, Perth Glory and A-Leagues have all been contacted for comment.

Perth-based football podcast and digital channel The Far Post Perth shared the original post, adding its own demand for intervention.

'Not a good look at all and something needs to be done about the problem at this point, genuine supporters are being impacted,' the account wrote.

One commenter alleged the group had been moving through the venue during the match while being followed by security and police.

'This is the mob that was walking back and forth all game with security/police following,' they wrote.

'We don't need this at HBF Park. It makes many people feel unsafe when these wannabe thugs just shove their way through.'

Another video shows young people confronting fans on the street outside nearby businesses

Photographs of damaged fences and other property have fuelled calls for stronger action

The person who posted the footage claimed that 'after the game the police and security were nowhere to be seen'.

They also shared a separate video from February, alleging it showed an earlier confrontation involving the same group.

The February post had complained about people attending matches in The Bay supporter area and allegedly fighting with other young spectators.

The complaints follow a strongly worded statement issued last year by supporter groups The Bay Perth and Shed End Perth, which demanded sanctions after a separate incident outside Gate 2 during the second half of a match at HBF Park.

The groups said they were aware of footage circulating online and distanced themselves from those involved, alleging physical confrontations had become a recurring problem.

'We want to make it absolutely clear that those involved are not fans and do not represent our supporter groups, our values, or the wider football community,' their joint statement read.

'These individuals consistently attend matches with the sole intention of causing problems rather than supporting the team, and their behaviour is completely unacceptable.'

The statement alleged confrontations had occurred in active supporter areas and the Eastern family stand, extending the groups' concerns beyond the stadium's most vocal sections.

Images shared alongside the complaints show fighting on previous occasions

'In almost every single game, they have caused physical confrontations in both the Active areas, and in some cases the Eastern family stand too, and it is deeply frustrating that this behaviour continues without meaningful consequences,' the groups said.

They alleged the behaviour was damaging the experience of supporters who attended matches to follow Perth Glory.

The groups also accused matchday security provider NPB Security of failing to respond adequately to incidents.

Their criticism included allegations that a rotating contingent of inexperienced security staff was being deployed and that personnel were unable or unwilling to intervene when serious problems arose.

'The lack of accountability from NPB Security is unacceptable and has undermined the safety of the matchday environment,' the statement read.

'Warnings and passive responses are clearly not working.'

The groups called for bans and other sanctions, warning that further incidents could affect spectators and people working at the ground.

'Without firm action, including bans and real consequences, these so-called 'fans' will continue to put genuine supporters, families, and staff at risk.'

They urged the club and stadium authorities to identify those responsible and impose firm sanctions.

Their earlier warning has been followed by fresh complaints about how security rules are enforced at Perth Glory matches.

'Meanwhile security go OTT about bottled water in the shed or actual fans taking t-shirts off,' one supporter wrote in response to the latest footage.

Another commenter similarly complained that removing a shirt in the supporter bay could result in ejection, while alleging people involved in violence escaped consequences.

The Far Post Perth also challenged a response that dismissed the latest incident as 'kids being kids'.

'Kids being kids is vandalising other people's property? Interesting,' the account replied, referring to the allegations of property damage.

However, one person responding to the original footage questioned whether those shown in the street were Perth Glory supporters.

'In the second video, the person filming is standing where the stadium is. These idiots look like they are walking from the other side of the road,' the commenter wrote.

'Are we sure they are even Glory fans? Or just troublemakers.'

The person who uploaded the footage insisted they were, although the posts do not establish that the same individuals were involved in each of the incidents raised by commenters.

The Bay Perth and Shed End Perth had made their position on violence explicit in their earlier appeal for action.

'Violence, fighting, and antisocial behaviour have no place in football,' they said.

'HBF Park, The Shed, The Bay and all areas of the ground should be a safe and welcoming environment for all supporters, families, players, and staff.'

That situation has reportedly encouraged Everton to examine their options ahead of January, with Oskarsson among the forwards attracting attention.

The Iceland international joined Real Sociedad from FC Copenhagen in 2024 and made progress during his previous campaign, scoring nine goals in LaLiga. His combination of physical presence, technical ability and finishing has helped establish him as an appealing prospect for clubs looking to strengthen their attacking ranks.

Oskarsson has also continued to impress at international level, with his performances for Iceland adding to his growing reputation. At 22, he could offer Everton both an immediate option up front and a potential long-term investment.

However, Everton would need to establish whether Real Sociedad are prepared to negotiate during the January window. The Spanish club invested significantly to secure his services, and there is no confirmation that they would be willing to let him leave midway through the season.

Oskarsson could be an important addition for Everton as Moyes looks to address the lack of depth at centre-forward. Relying heavily on Barry leaves the manager with limited specialist alternatives, particularly across a demanding second half of the campaign.

The Icelandic striker’s profile could suit Everton’s need for another option capable of leading the line. His technical qualities may also give Moyes greater flexibility in how the team approaches matches, while his age offers scope for further development.

Competition from Tottenham, Newcastle, Sunderland and Brentford could complicate Everton’s pursuit, however. The Toffees would need to move decisively if their interest develops into a formal approach, while the final cost and Sociedad’s willingness to sell would be key factors.

For now, Everton’s reported interest suggests the club are assessing potential solutions ahead of January rather than confirming a deal is imminent. With Moyes needing greater depth in attack, Oskarsson is a name to watch as the winter transfer window approaches.

#1667. Germany 5-0 Netherlands: Wirtz stars as Klopp’s side hit best form to top group

By Axel Clody | 17 Nov 2026 06:25

Germany thrashed the Netherlands 5-0 on Monday at the Olympiastadion in Berlin in the final round of the Nations League group stage.

In a convincing performance, the four-time world champions produced their best football since the arrival of Jurgen Klopp, who took charge of the national team after the disappointing 2026 World Cup campaign.

With goals from Derry Scherhant, Nico Schlotterbeck, Brajan Gruda and Florian Wirtz, who scored twice, the Germans produced an impressive result against opponents who were also fighting for top spot in the group.

The victory took on even greater importance because of the situation before the match. Germany began the round in third place in Group A2, level on points with Greece and behind the Dutch, and risked missing out on the quarter-finals. With the win, they reached 11 points, overtook their rivals on goal difference and finished the first phase at the top, securing a place among the best eight in the competition.

One of the stars of the night was Derry Scherhant. Klopp’s selection on the left of the attack scored his first goal for the senior Germany team.

A native of Berlin, the 24-year-old winger, who plays for Freiburg, took the opportunity to make his mark in front of the crowd of his home city. His exuberant celebration after finding the top corner past Bart Verbruggen reflected the special significance of the moment in his international career.

The goal also rewarded the faith the manager has placed in the attacker. Scherhant was only making his fourth appearance for the national team and has earned his place amid the renewal carried out by Klopp since he took over.

The chance given to the Freiburg player is part of a strategy that seeks to widen the squad’s options, without restricting selections to the best-known names in German football. Against the Netherlands, the youngster delivered and showed that he can be an interesting option in attack.

Another standout was Wirtz, who again showed how his talent can make a difference in a Germany shirt. The attacking midfielder scored twice in the second half and was decisive in turning a lead built before the break into a rout. His ability to find space, accelerate attacks and arrive in positions to shoot gave another dimension to the German attack.

The performance reinforces one of the main positive certainties of the early days of Klopp’s reign: Wirtz is capable of taking on the team’s technical leadership.

As well as the brilliance of the number 17 and Scherhant’s first goal, the match also underlined the importance of the opportunities given to other young players. Gruda, who had already scored in the 3-1 win over Serbia, found the net again during this international break and has now scored two goals for the national team.

Left-back Philipp Treu was also among the starters, benefiting from the opening up of opportunities by the manager. These are names that help to give shape to a project still under construction and show that Klopp intends to increase competition in different positions.

It was a well-played and competitive first half, with good link-up play and quick transitions. At home, Germany had more possession and went for a proactive game, with a high line and patience to find space.

In the 41st minute, they found it: Scherhant received the ball on the right, got past Denzel Dumfries and curled a lovely shot across goal into the top corner past Verbruggen.

The Netherlands, for their part, took to the pitch practically already qualified. In their tactical approach in the first half, the Dutch opted for a more reactive game: either Xavi Hernandez’s team reached dangerous areas through counter-attacks, or they drew in the German press and built from the back, passing the ball patiently.

At the start of the second half, Germany needed only a few minutes to punish the visitors again. Fourteen minutes into the half, Wirtz began a move down the left, tried to play a one-two with Scherhant, but saw Dumfries step in front of him. The Liverpool midfielder then regained the ball, dribbled past the Dutch full-back and struck hard with his left foot from the edge of the area to make it 2-0.

From there it became a stroll. The Netherlands clearly felt the blow, and the hosts took advantage to turn the win into a rout. Schlotterbeck, with a header, Wirtz, with another stunning goal, and Gruda gave the match its final numbers.

#1665. GdS: Worth the price tag – how Moreira became ‘untouchable’ for Milan and Belgium

It has been a positive international break for Diego Moreira, who continued his excellent form from club football.

As La Gazzetta dello Sport write this morning, Ruben Amorim will welcome Moreira back to Milanello soon. The winger has become a regular starter and producing goals and assists, but the Portuguese coach knows the pitfalls of the match against Frosinone all too well.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Therefore, starting Thursday – when the squad will be fully back together after the day off tomorrow – everyone’s minds will be focused solely on the new busy schedule awaiting the Rossoneri until Christmas. More specifically, seven matches from Sunday until December 19th.

Immediately after the last international break, the Rossoneri drew away to Sassuolo, a result that certainly wasn’t greeted with a smile. The goal is to avoid repeating that misstep against Alvini’s team, and Moreira will be key to that.

Despite his 22 years of age and the €50m valuation plus bonuses that could have weighed heavily on his shoulders, Diego hasn’t taken long to win over Milan fans. In his last six league matches (he missed two due to injury), he’s scored four goals and provided three assists.

He has also demonstrated his ability to switch roles with ease, playing as a winger on the right or left, as a wing-back or even as a full-back. He plays with the boldness of someone who targets his opponent and tries to dribble past him, something that fans always appreciate.

Moreira always seeks one-on-one situations, both due to his strengths and the explicit request of Amorim, who asks his wide players to create numerical superiority. Diego is succeeding remarkably, as his assist for Christian Pulisic in the derby shows, as he got past Carlo Augusto and crossed.

Moreira made the difference against Italy on Sunday too: not only did he score the fourth goal, which he celebrated by making a gesture of ‘one, two, three and four’ with his fingers, but he also kept accelerating, hit the woodwork, shot wide once more and had two shots blocked by his opponents.

He set up De Bruyne for a shot, had more touches than anyone else in the opponents’ area (11) and often took on Calafiori and Dimarco, delighting the crowd with a spectacular backheel. He had around 50 touches and 27/31 completed passes, earning the applause of the entire stadium when he came off.

Moreira is currently captivating thanks to his drive and desire. He’s that way at Milan and he’s that way with the national team. That’s why there’s a version of the Rossoneri with him and another without him which, frankly, isn’t as threatening.

Amorim carefully integrated him into the team’s operations at the start of the season, but now he has broken the padlock off and now considers him a key player in the team. This doesn’t mean he won’t need a breather, given the schedule, but the coach will have to think about the right moments to rest.

With four goals in Serie A (one every 121 minutes), he’s already matched his four goals from last season in Ligue 1, and he has no intention of stopping. He feels the confidence in himself and the team.

The leap from Ligue 1 to Serie A didn’t bother him. In fact, he intends to continue dancing on the pitch, just like in the derby or against Italy. On Sunday, he wants to show he has the same energy with which he brought Italy to its knees. Milan and San Siro await him.

#1664. Milos Kerkez isn't the problem at Liverpool, there's a far bigger one

Milos Kerkez isn't the problem that many think he is at Liverpool. Instead, there's a far bigger one and Andoni Iraola has got to fix it.

Milos Kerkez has been getting stick this season as he's struggled for form. He's far from alone in that, of course, but the left-back has looked quite shaky at the back while offering little going forward.

He does, in his defence, have to take on an incredibly difficult task as the long-term replacement for Andy Robertson. Robertson is by far the best left-back Liverpool have had in 30 years and one of the greatest to ever play in the Premier League.

Some could argue that it was a bizarre decision to force him out and move on when he's still clearly capable of delivering at the top level. But it's a little late for that - Kerkez is now the first-choice left-back.

A bigger problem for Kerkez is that he's not in an environment built for success. In fact, his job is incredibly difficult and one that Andoni Iraola has to help with. Because as things stand, we'll never see the best of him.

Liverpool's bigger problemShape. Liverpool’s shape is a sight to behold and one that you can see quite clearly anytime you watch them: because it doesn’t really change. The Reds are unbelievably static going forward, with very little attacking movement. They have a left-winger, a right-winger, a centre-forward and a no.10 - none of whom really interchange. The centre of the pitch doesn’t really offer space for wingers to run into. The effect of that is a clogged wing, too, which essentially always has a winger sticking wide on it. And the effect of that? Kerkez doesn’t have much space to run into. Virtually all his attacking chances come on the overlap in a short space, usually needing to fire a cross into a crowded box.

Shape. Liverpool’s shape is a sight to behold and one that you can see quite clearly anytime you watch them: because it doesn’t really change.

The Reds are unbelievably static going forward, with very little attacking movement. They have a left-winger, a right-winger, a centre-forward and a no.10 - none of whom really interchange.

The centre of the pitch doesn’t really offer space for wingers to run into. The effect of that is a clogged wing, too, which essentially always has a winger sticking wide on it.

And the effect of that? Kerkez doesn’t have much space to run into. Virtually all his attacking chances come on the overlap in a short space, usually needing to fire a cross into a crowded box.

Above we've got Kerkez's heatmap this season. As you can see, it's almost symmetrical along the halfway line. Kerkez gets lots of his touches within Liverpool's half, with the rest coming from deep in the attacking half.

Things taper out towards the opposition box, with no defined path actually to and around the attacking box. So let's have a look at Robertson's at Tottenham.

Isn't that different? Robertson has actually had more touches than Kerkez but the spread of his touches is far more diverse. His touches in the attacking half are much more present than those in his own, while you can see that clear, consistent path into the opposition box.

Robertson looks like an attacking full-back here. One who has a consistent path down the flank but also has space to move inside. Kerkez has neither.

And there's another factor. As mentioned, Robertson has had more touches - 625 to Kerkez's 565. The kicker here, though, is that the Liverpool full-back has played much more than his former teammate.

Kerkez has 825 Premier League minutes this season. Robertson has just 668. 157 fewer minutes, so we’re coming up to two full matches worth there. Yet the Scot is far more involved.

Offensively, anyway. Liverpool’s setup, leaving Kerkez deeper, has the knock-on effect of asking him to do much, much more defending than someone like Robertson.

Kerkez faces twice as many aerial duels and around three times as many duels overall. That’s despite the fact Spurs haven’t started the season well and aren’t exactly a team that rarely defends.

But Liverpool are not setup to play to Kerkez’s strengths. He’s not allowed room to attack and has essentially been cast as a defensive full-back - something he can’t really do. Until that changes, he will look sub-par.

#1661. The unexpected email that led to Bukayo Saka's Socrates Award win at the Ballon d'Or: Inside Arsenal star's secret humanitarian work after his surprise win at London ceremony

Published: 08:07 EST, 11 November 2026 | Updated: 08:13 EST, 11 November 2026

The sight of Bukayo Saka hobbling down the red carpet at the Ballon d'Or ceremony came as a surprise. Only those closest to him knew why he was there, and the years of toil that led to this moment.

While his England team-mate Harry Kane claimed the night's top on-pitch prize, Saka – who had suffered a thigh injury just days before against Kane's Bayern Munich – was at the London Palladium to collect the Socrates Award for his humanitarian work.

Joining a roll of honour that includes previous winners Vinicius Junior, Sadio Mane and Luis Enrique, Saka walked onto the stage, reached into his suit pocket and read a letter from a 14-year-old boy in Rwanda whose eyesight had been restored through his charity work.

Now, Daily Mail Sport can reveal the scale of the Arsenal star's involvement over the last four years with the BigShoe charity, which funds operations, feeds children and helps with disaster relief across the world. From restoring the eyesight of that 14-year-old in Rwanda to helping provide life-saving procedures for 120 children in Nigeria, Saka's impact goes far beyond the stadiums he dazzles in.

And this is no passive act of philanthropy. BigShoe president Valerie Fiesser's phone is often inundated with messages from Saka when the charity is delivering projects in poverty-stricken countries such as Nigeria and Rwanda. Many of the project ideas come from the 25-year-old himself.

'Bukayo is really, really productive,' Fiesser tells Daily Mail Sport. 'He is really pushing how he wants to help. I think for him it is never fast enough to help. Sometimes Bukayo comes up with projects and he says, "Shouldn't we help here?" So he is really interested in it. It is not like he is just sending money and saying, "OK, nice, we'll do a project in Nigeria".

Bukayo Saka was handed the Ballon d'Or Socrates Award for his humanitarian work last month

Saka has worked with BigShoe charity for years - helping those in poverty-stricken countries

In 2023, Saka donated 50 containers to help provide shelter for 255 people impacted by the devastating earthquake in Morocco

'When we are on the ground, he is texting, "Is everything alright? Is everybody safe? Are all the children safe? Which services do we have? Can I see pictures? Send me pictures, send me pictures, send me pictures!"

BigShoe, a German-based charity founded during the 2006 World Cup, began years ago by funding life-changing surgery for Nourisson, a young girl from Togo born with a cleft lip and palate. The Togo national team, playing at their first World Cup, were based in the city of Wangen im Allgau, which brought the story to prominence in Germany.

The charity is now a worldwide network of football stars, fans and partners, with more than 10,000 children around the globe having benefitted via projects ranging from medical supplies to shelter and food. The organisation has also worked with Antonio Rudiger, Paul Pogba and Saka's ex-Arsenal team-mates Mesut Ozil and Oleksandr Zinchenko.

Fiesser vividly remembers how Saka first got in touch, in early 2022.

'He just really randomly wrote us an email,' she says. 'He asked us if we can help together in Nigeria after seeing a project of another soccer player. He said, "I want to help children, I want to help people and can we do something". (It was) really just random.'

That initial conversation quickly developed into a project in late 2022 which funded 120 life-changing medical operations for children in Nigeria. Some of the youngsters were suffering from brain tumours, while others required treatment for hernias.

'This was an incredible project because it was the first project in Nigeria together with him,' she says. 'It was really life-changing for the children because some had a brain tumour, some had hernia problems.'

Saka has since helped support healthcare check-ups for more than 580 children in Rwanda and provide disaster relief after devastating earthquakes in Morocco and Turkey, while his involvement has extended far beyond financial backing.

The charity is now a worldwide network of football stars, fans and partners, with more than 10,000 kids having benefitted via projects ranging from medical supplies to shelter and food

'We did a disaster relief where we provided homes for the earthquake victims in Morocco and Turkey and he was asking questions like, "Do they have electricity there?"' she says.

'He is really thinking, "Is it worth it, does it make sense to do this, or is it just putting the container and then the people do not have water and they cannot live there?" So he is really, really smart. And yes, I think he is an amazing human.

'It was never about him. It was always about the children and how we can help. It was never like, "OK, we are talking to one of the best players of the world." I think he is raised like this. His family made him the man he is now.

'I think he is raised like this, that you have to be a good human being and to help others and just have an impact in life.'

Saka and his family are directly involved in the projects, identifying communities in need and deciding exactly how support should be delivered. His mother, Adenike, is a key figure.

'We decide together where we can help, how we can help and then we actually help together,' Fiesser says. 'Me and his mother WhatsApp, call regularly. She has played a big part and is a driving force.

'Three months ago we renovated a school in Rwanda and we provided them with water filters for clean drinking water. We also built girls' changing rooms, a new soccer pitch and a new library. Bukayo's family was on the ground, twice.

'We decided after we saw that the families are really hungry in this area to do food packages. It is our next project in November and December.

'He (Saka) really wants to make a difference. He wants to change lives.'

While Saka will continue to chase trophies in Arsenal red and England white, his greatest legacy may ultimately be measured in the lives he has changed far beyond the football pitch.

#1659. "Magical" - German media rave over Liverpool star Florian Wirtz after 5-0 win vs the Netherlands

By Lewis Blain | 17 Nov 2026 07:18, Last updated: 17 Nov 2026 07:24

Germany continued their impressive progress under former Liverpool boss Jurgen Klopp with a commanding 5-0 victory over the Netherlands in the UEFA Nations League on Monday evening, with Florian Wirtz producing a standout performance.

The Reds midfielder scored twice in his 50th international appearance, including a spectacular left-footed effort, as Germany recorded their biggest victory over their neighbours since 1959.

Wirtz's display earned widespread praise in his homeland, with several publications awarding him the highest possible grade on the German school-style marking system, where 1 is the best, and 6 is the worst.

SPORT1 awarded Wirtz 1/6, describing his performance as "Ein magischer Abend des Hoffnungsträgers" - a 'magical' evening from the team's star of hope.

The publication acknowledged that he initially struggled to influence proceedings but praised his response after the interval, highlighting his spectacular first goal, subsequent brace-completing finish and ability to dictate Germany's attacking play. Sport Bild also hailed the Liverpool star's 'magic' on an impressive night.

FOCUS Online and Eurosport Germany also awarded Wirtz 1/6, with the latter describing him as the "überragende Mann" - the 'outstanding' player - after his two goals and impressive work out of possession.

FOCUS were particularly impressed by his response to an imperfect moment, joking that he had once dribbled the ball out of play unchallenged before showing his true quality with a "superb brace".

The Frankfurter Rundschau also handed him 1/6, describing him as the "Dreh- und Angelpunkt im Offensivspiel" - the 'focal point' of Germany's attacking play - while suggesting Klopp's system was allowing him to flourish.

Märkische Oderzeitung were slightly less generous, awarding Wirtz 1.5/6, but still praised his technical quality and two excellent finishes. They noted that he initially struggled to find decisive openings before becoming increasingly influential after the hour mark.

Sportschau did not provide a rating but similarly acknowledged that Wirtz was relatively subdued during the first half, before writing that he "Krönte seinen immer stärkeren Auftritt dann mit zwei Treffern" - capped his 'increasingly influential performance' with two goals.

The German media's enthusiasm inevitably raises the question of whether Wirtz can reproduce his international form more consistently at Anfield heading into a busy festive period.

There is little doubt that the 23-year-old has shown encouraging signs during his second season at Liverpool, registering two goals and five assists in 15 appearances across all competitions. However, these returns are still considerably below the extraordinary numbers he produced during his time at Bayer Leverkusen.

Wirtz registered 35 goals and 44 assists in 140 Bundesliga appearances for Leverkusen, becoming one of Europe's most exciting attacking midfielders. While adapting to English football and the Reds' demands takes time, he has yet to consistently reach those same creative and goalscoring heights for his club.

There have been encouraging developments, including scoring and assisting in their 3-1 victory over Crystal Palace on November 8th, but the German's international performances are increasingly setting the benchmark for what supporters will expect.

His next opportunity to demonstrate that improvement comes in a huge Premier League encounter, with Liverpool welcoming Manchester United to Anfield on Sunday 22nd November.

After producing two goals against the Netherlands and earning a near-unanimous collection of top marks in Germany, Wirtz will return to Merseyside with considerable confidence. Klopp's influence on the national team has also provided an encouraging reminder of the football that Wirtz can produce when operating with freedom and confidence.

Liverpool will hope that his international brilliance can become a more regular feature at club level, particularly with one of their biggest fixtures of the season approaching.

#1656. Di Marzio: Endrick and Tresoldi deals ‘not a financial issue’ for Milan – the situation

AC Milan have the financial capability to go out and sign their top targets in January, according to Gianluca Di Marzio.

Several reports and even the words of owner Gerry Cardinale have made it very clear that Milan plan to be busy in the winter mercato. The main target seems to be a forward to complete the attack, as well as a centre-back to help out the defensive department too.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Among the names linked have been Real Madrid’s Endrick, Club Brugge’s Nicolo Tresoldi and Sporting CP’s Goncalo Inacio. It’s one thing having the list of names, but it is another having the money and the possibility of doing a deal mid-season with the selling club.

During last night’s segment on Sky, Gianluca Di Marzio (via MilanNews) was asked whether Milan can realistically pursue names like Endrick and Tresoldi, who are likely to cost over €50m each.

“That they has the strength to do these kinds of deals, yes. They demonstrated it over the summer, so I don’t think there’s a financial issue,” he began.

“Whether they manage to sign one of the two… Endrick, as far as we know, José Mourinho hasn’t changed his mind and therefore doesn’t intend to part with him in January. But Endrick is a Cardinale obsession, just as he was a Roma obsession during the summer.

“We’ll have to see if Mourinho changes his mind in the month and a half before the transfer window opens. He hasn’t changed his mind at the moment, so I see the situation as complicated at the moment.

“Just as it’s complicated for Brugge to sell Tresoldi. Brugge are a club that doesn’t need to sell and always sells at least one key player in the summer, precisely to try to get to the end of the season with its players.

“Milan are looking for a striker, looking for a back-up for Ramos. The figures I’ve read, 60-70 million, are very, very high figures to try to convince Brugge to sell him. It’s a deal that – given the player’s objective value – I think is around 50 million. In my opinion.

“But Brugge are unlikely to sell him in January. Above all, Milan is looking for a striker to be a back-up for Ramos; it’s not like Ramos and Tresoldi will play together. In the sense that Milan has always played with a centre-forward.

“Above all, they need to provide this center forward with plenty of playable balls rather than buy another. Because if Ramos doesn’t receive balls in the penalty area, he struggles to score, and Tresoldi struggles to score either.

“They need a striker to get Camarda playing. I think Camarda will go and play and therefore an investment will be needed in a player who can be a suitable deputy for Ramos.”

#1655. Man United transfer news: Former defender backs move for Chelsea star Estevao

By Axel Clody | 17 Nov 2026 08:02

Mikael Silvestre sees Estevao as a player capable of strengthening Manchester United, but does not believe the Red Devils will pursue the forward at this time.

The former France defender, who played for the Old Trafford club between 1999 and 2008, praised the Brazilian’s performance and considered him an interesting option if he were available on the market. However, that prospect hinges on the young player’s willingness to fight for his place at Stamford Bridge.

Silvestre’s assessment comes at a time of significant change at Manchester United. The club invested more than £144m (€170m) in signings last summer and showed an intention to back Michael Carrick after the team finished last season in third place in the Premier League. The start of the new campaign, however, has fallen short of expectations.

The enthusiasm that had arisen among the fans was quickly replaced by dissatisfaction with the results. After the 2-0 defeat away to Chelsea, Manchester United reached nine consecutive matches without a win in all competitions. Neither the reaction against Roma, with a comeback in the Europa League, nor the 4-4 draw with Aston Villa at Old Trafford was enough to prevent the departure of Carrick, who was sacked last Thursday (12 November).

Mauricio Pochettino has been chosen to take charge of the team. The Argentinian has officially left the United States national team and is expected to begin work at Manchester United this week, while the board is already focusing its attention on the January transfer window.

Among the possibilities to strengthen the squad, Estevao appears as a name that appeals to Silvestre. The 19-year-old Brazilian is still seeking greater playing time at Chelsea, but he had a standout performance precisely against Manchester United at Stamford Bridge.

In an interview with Betarades.gr, the former player highlighted the forward’s display and pointed to his determination as an obstacle to a possible transfer.

‘Estevao played for Chelsea against Manchester United, and I think he showed why he deserves more playing time. It looks like he is going to fight for his place, so I do not think Manchester United will make a move for him’ - Silvestre said.

The Frenchman’s interpretation is that the Brazilian intends to seize opportunities to establish himself at Chelsea rather than seek a move at this time. Even so, Silvestre left no doubt about his individual assessment of the player.

‘But he is definitely a good player. He plays for the Brazil national team, and I like his style of play. If he were available for transfer, he would be a good signing for Manchester United’ - he added.

Manchester United are set to return to the transfer market in January with the intention of improving the team’s performance in the second half of the season. One of their priorities is signing a left-back, a position for which the club unsuccessfully attempted to sign Lewis Hall from Newcastle in the summer.

The attacking department may also receive attention from the board. Bryan Mbeumo and Matheus Cunha, considered important players for the team, have had starts to the season below expectations, increasing the need to find alternatives in attack.

With Pochettino about to begin his tenure, planning for the next transfer window is gaining importance. Estevao, despite having Silvestre’s approval, would depend on a change of scenery at Chelsea to effectively enter Manchester United’s radar.

For now, the most likely scenario is that the Brazilian will remain in London trying to gain more playing time and consolidate his position at Chelsea.
